question: At an equal measurement budget N, does the choice of which channels to measure change the estimation error?
claim: Information-gain (D-optimal) selection beats uniform spacing at equal N.
arms: A_random: draw N channels uniformly at random without replacement; the draw is derived from the seed so it is reproducible
B_uniform: place N channels at equal spacing across the available range
C_infogain: greedy D-optimal; add the channel that most reduces the log-determinant of the posterior covariance, using only the reference model and the design regularisation, never the observations
metric_definition_point: the err() function in the scoring module of the measurement lane - one definition, referenced by every arm
decision_rule: Paired per seed: d_s = err_C(s) - err_B(s). Bootstrap the mean of d_s over 10000 resamples of the seeds with the rng seed fixed here, and take the 2.5/97.5 percentiles as a 95% CI. Run-to-run variability is the median of the three per-arm seed-wise MADs. Only C against B is judged; A is plotted and never scored.
win_conditions: the bootstrap 95% CI of the mean of d_s does not cross zero
stop_conditions: any budget has missing trials: do not score, report the gap
at N equal to the full channel count the arms must agree, because every arm then uses every channel; if they disagree the harness is wrong and nothing is scored
if only one of the two win conditions holds, the verdict is 'no difference'; a near miss is not reread as a win
controls: A_random is carried through the whole run so that the two designed arms are visible against an undesigned one
the full-budget agreement check above is a control on the harness, not on the claim
